surface_verification.justification: No startable product surface: CI test modules plus one scanner scope-exclusion file. The behaviour introduced IS the gate's own pass/fail, verified in its FAILING direction — 15 drift mutations on the real tree, all RED, suite green after every restore, run with the modules TRACKED. Evidence: iterate-2026-08-01-semgrep-suppression-ratchet/ac7-falsification.md.

behaviors.behavior: Live .semgrepignore pattern set equals the pinned registry (disk->registry)
...and registry->disk
Every scope pattern carries a >=40-char rationale
Blanket server/scripts/ exclusion gone; copy-assets.mjs in scope; the three non-shipped files out
Inline directive set equals the pinned registry, both directions
...including exact per-pair COUNTS
Every inline suppression carries a >=40-char rationale
A directive that names no rule is rejected
The legacy short stem is detected, not just the long one
Multi-rule directives register each id separately
A malformed rule id voids the whole directive rather than partly parsing
The marker is not matched inside a longer token
Python is read line by line, so a marker in a STRING is not skipped
A marker in a TS string literal IS reported (the deliberate fail-safe trade)
Each of the four supported .semgrepignore shapes classifies correctly
Every unsupported shape is REJECTED, not misread
Anchoring and any-depth matching behave as gitignore does
live_patterns ignores comments and blank lines
Scope filter and directive scan compose on a real git tree
A new file type in scan scope must be classified
Discovery cannot pass vacuously on an empty set
The guard does not report its own source as a suppression (AC-8)
behaviors.evidence: full scripts/ci/tests suite 309 PASSED with all seven modules tracked

An extensionless file with a shebang IS scanned
Basename matching is case-SENSITIVE (same verdict on Windows and Linux CI)
UnsupportedPattern tells the developer what to do

behaviors.behavior: A BARE marker earlier on the line voids the whole directive (blanket form)
A second block-comment directive on one line is not discarded
PROSE_EXEMPT cannot become a self-service bypass (vendored-only, rule-less-only, count-pinned)
The scanner's INVOCATION cannot be narrowed outside .semgrepignore
A nested .semgrepignore cannot silence a subtree unseen
A scanned language cannot be relabelled 'not a Semgrep language'
Deleting a ratchet module cannot leave the directory run green
A Dockerfile (name-detected, no extension, no shebang) is scanned
The vendored module's prose does not register and a real directive does (AC-6)
